title: Custom Door Handle Flashlight
overview: Door handle with an integrated flashlight developed with WPI MakerBucks support, combining custom electronics with compact mechanical packaging.
scope: Electronics housing design, rotary-encoder-based lighting controls, component stacking and integration, and functional testing.
materials:
• A 3D-printed PLA sleeve (electronics housing)
 • A rotary encoder (for on/off click and brightness dimming)
 • A single 18650 lithium-ion cell
 • A microcontroller
 • An LED ring (attempted; not fully functional in v1)
 • A capacitive touch sensor (attempted; not fully functional in v1)
 • A donor door handle (for reference and final mounting)
fabricationSteps:
1. Research how a standard flashlight is put together (components and layout) to establish a working reference design.
 2. Design the internal electronics housing to fit inside a door-handle form factor.
 3. Choose a rotary encoder to serve double duty: click for on/off, twist for brightness dimming.
 4. Stack all electronics — microcontroller, driver circuitry, main LED, ring light, and battery holder — inside a single 3D-printed PLA sleeve.
 5. Wire a single 18650 cell to power the microcontroller, main light, and LED ring.
 6. Press-fit and glue the stacked components together inside the sleeve for the version-1 build.
 7. Test all functions: the main light and dimming worked as intended; the ring light and capacitive touch sensor did not work reliably in this version.
outcome: Delivered a working proof-of-concept flashlight handle, with an aluminum-machined version planned to improve durability and thermal performance.
